statement: the paper introduces and describes new microscopic LHAR test structures for analysing ALD conformality
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: ALD draws wide interest for its unmatched conformality, which results from self-terminating gas-solid reactions
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: the LHAR structures are all-silicon rectangular channels whose roof is held up by pillars
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: aspect ratios beyond 10 000:1 keep the adsorption front from reaching the channel end, so the saturation profile is exposed for analysis
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: TMA-water alumina ALD is used as a test vehicle to show that saturation profile measurement is applicable, repeatable and reproducible, and as a benchmark for later studies
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: longer or shorter TMA pulses and purges revealed new details of how TMA-water ALD chemisorbs and of its surface chemistry
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: new classifications and terms for saturation profiles are proposed, meant for other LHAR studies and partly also for CVD and ALE
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: conformality: the ability to cover a 3D object with a homogeneous coating of even thickness
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: conformal coatings are needed in electronics, heterogeneous catalysis, biosensors and energy applications
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: ALD, a CVD variant, was invented independently more than forty years ago as atomic layer epitaxy and molecular layering; Tuomo Suntola received the Millennium Technology Prize in 2018
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: ALD offers film thickness control below one nanometre through self-terminating reactions that stop by themselves
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: even ALD does not guarantee conformal coating at a given aspect ratio, so process parameters must be tuned for HAR structures
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: in ideal ALD, how deep the coating reaches grows as the square root of reactant dose
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: dose = reactant partial pressure times exposure time; in this work the partial pressure is not strictly constant, so dose need not grow linearly with pulse time
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: reactivity, often given as a lumped sticking coefficient c_A, sets how fast uniform thickness is reached; CVD from decomposition or pulse mixing, or unsaturated reactions, harm conformality
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: vertical HAR structures etched in silicon, analysed by SEM or TEM after careful preparation, have been the practical industry standard for conformality
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: step coverage: ratio of bottom film thickness to top film thickness of a feature
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: lumped sticking coefficients have sometimes been extracted from the often sparse VHAR data
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: in LHAR analysis the channel roof is taken off after ALD so the film can be examined from the top with methods for planar surfaces
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: LHAR features are usually made so deep that the film does not reach their end, which allows analysis of the saturation profile
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Dendooven et al. assembled macroscopic rectangular LHAR channels with heights in the hundreds of micrometres
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Gao et al. microfabricated LHAR cavities (Si bottom, polysilicon roof, SiO2 pillars) with design heights of 200, 500 or 1000 nm and ARs above 10 000:1; called PillarHall-1 here
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Schwille et al. built centrosymmetric MEMS-like LHAR cavities with a limiting gap height of 4.5 µm
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: improved microscopic rectangular LHAR channels derived from the Gao process were used before but not described in detail
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: only a small minority of over 700 published ALD processes have had their conformality studied in LHAR structures
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: processes studied in LHAR so far: Al2O3 from TMA/H2O, TiO2 from TiCl4/H2O, Ir and IrOx from Ir(acac)3, HfSiOx, SiO2 with O3, and PEALD of Al2O3, AlN, SiO2, TiO2 and HfO2
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: LHAR studies usually fit a reversible or irreversible single-site Langmuir adsorption model to the saturation profile to get a lumped sticking coefficient
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Dendooven et al. extracted the TMA sticking coefficient on Al2O3 and its effect on step coverage, and used Monte Carlo with LHAR for PEALD Al2O3 and AlN
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Schwille et al. obtained sticking coefficients of TMA and BDEAS from Monte Carlo simulation combined with LHAR data
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Ylilammi et al. obtained lumped sticking coefficients of TMA on Al2O3 and TiCl4 on TiO2 with a diffusion-reaction model of LHAR profiles
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Arts et al. took the lumped sticking coefficient from the profile slope, and O2 plasma radical recombination probabilities from PEALD penetration depth
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: TMA-water was chosen because it is near-ideal, already studied in LHAR, and its surface chemistry and kinetics are still debated
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: the authors hope that CVD, ALE and other ALD processes can later be compared against this TMA-water benchmark
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: the ALD Al2O3 films of this work were grown at 300 °C, the temperature most used for TMA-water
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: four saturation profile classes are proposed (as-measured, scaled, Type 1 and Type 2 normalized); each has been used in the literature, also in combination
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: as-measured saturation profile: total growth (nm, ng, nm-2, ...) against distance x (µm), straight from the measurement
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Dendooven et al. and Ylilammi et al. showed process-parameter effects on PEALD and ALD conformality with as-measured profiles
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: scaled saturation profile: growth per cycle (nm, ng, nm-2, ...) against the dimensionless distance
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: dimensionless distance x~ = x/H, measurement distance over channel height (unitless)
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: earlier works often used the aspect ratio as horizontal axis where this work uses the dimensionless distance
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: x~ stays fixed however much film grows, while the aspect ratio felt by the process rises as the film narrows the channel
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Type 1 normalized profile: growth with its channel-entrance value set to 1 against x~
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: the normalized growth may be read as surface coverage θ, with 0 ≤ θ ≤ 1
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Arts et al. get a lumped sticking coefficient from the slope of the Type 1 profile when the mean free path greatly exceeds the limiting channel size and the excess number is below 0.1
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Type 2 normalized profile: normalized growth against the normalized distance
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: normalized distance ξ = x/L, distance over the channel lateral length (unitless)
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Yanguas-Gil et al. used the Type 2 profile to set criteria telling diffusion-limited from reaction-limited ALD
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: the profile is split into four regions; Region I lies outside, in front of the channel, i.e. on the planar substrate
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Region II starts at the channel entry (distance zero) and has roughly constant thickness from saturated reactions up to a knee
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: ideally thickness divided by cycles in Regions I and II gives the characteristic GPC
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Region III, after the knee, is where thickness falls because reactions are unsaturated; it is also called the adsorption front
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Region IV follows the adsorption front; thickness there should ideally be zero
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Region II has subregions a, b, c; a nanostep with slightly higher thickness is sometimes seen between IIa and IIb
author: 10.1039_d0cp03358h

statement: Region IIb is the early part after the nanostep where growth per cycle is at its saturated maximum (useful for modelling); IIc is the rest before the knee, and the IIb/IIc border may be arbitrary
